small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_OC tiles (e.g., 128) and try BLOCK_OH=1/BLOCK_OW=128 with num_warps=8 — OC=64 means current BLOCK_OC=64 covers all channels in one block, eliminating the OC grid dim and enabling larger spatial tiles per program.
- Cache the weight tile (BLOCK_OC × IC*KH*KW = 64×72 = 4608 floats) in registers/shared once at the top of the kernel, then iterate spatial; current code reloads w_vals BLOCK_OH*BLOCK_OW times per (ic,kh,kw). Restructure inner loop so weights are loaded as a 2D tile and reused across the spatial tile via tl.dot.
- Switch to channels_last (NHWC) input layout so the IC reduction is the contiguous axis, then use tl.dot on [BLOCK_SPATIAL, IC*KH*KW] × [IC*KH*KW, BLOCK_OC] GEMM tiles.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, output-spatial tile of size BM, OC tile of size BN=64), reducing over K=IC*KH*KW=72 via tl.dot. K=72 fits in a single BLOCK_K=72 (or pad to 96/128), so the inner loop becomes a single matmul rather than a triple-nested scalar accumulate — this is the main missing optimization vs. cuDNN.
- Fuse bias + subtract + Mish into the GEMM epilogue (already done), but compute Mish via the numerically-stable softplus `tl.where(x>20, x, log1p(exp(x)))` form and use `tanh` via `2*sigmoid(2x)-1` to avoid the redundant exp(2*sp) chain.
- Use NHWC layout end-to-end (permute input + weight once at init, store output NHWC then permute back, or even better keep output NHWC if downstream allows) so the K-dim load of the input patch is one contiguous vector per spatial point, dramatically improving L2 reuse for K=72.
